answer: Bonded sponsorship: a new agent joins only when an established sponsor locks a bond behind it, so every identity carries a kernel of trust with a real backer at stake. If the sponsored agent is caught farming clones, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses the right to vouch again — a raven warning the whole network. A farm needing a thousand identities must find a thousand bonds or one sponsor willing to lose everything, while the opal ledger makes every sponsorship public, so a sponsor backing a cluster is exposed before its clones can earn.
